pairs.subject: quality-gates
pairs.evidence: app/features/tools/devcases/DevProbeStrengthBanner.tsx:21 The approval-gate banner renders nothing for a case with zero probes, but enforceProbeGate (app/_lib/devcase-probe-audit.ts:88,113) treats zero probes as verdict none and refuses approval with a 422. The surface the reviewer reads before approving leaves out a condition that will block them.

techniques.evidence: app/features/tools/devcases/DevProbeStrengthBanner.tsx:21 The display understates the enforced policy. auditProbeStrength already returns none for total 0 and a t('none') headline exists, but the early return hides it. DevLifecycleReviewPanel.tsx:172 also wraps the banner in probes.length > 0, so the review screen shows nothing at all.

app/features/tools/devcases/DevTab.approve-error.test.ts:17 The guard matches raw source text with comments left in, so a comment can satisfy the presence regex for runAction('approve' (the permissive direction). The target file already explains the forbidden if (r.ok) form in a comment at useDevTabNeedAnalysis.ts:101.

app/features/tools/devcases/DevTab.approve-error.test.ts:29 The absence assertion keys on the variable name r. Writing if (res.ok) { or r.ok && ... brings back the dead-button pattern and the test stays green, and the test never says that its key can be renamed away.

app/features/tools/devcases/DevTab.approve-error.test.ts:20 The test checks that its instrument found its target before asserting anything. A renamed or removed approve() goes red rather than passing vacuously.
app/features/tools/devcases/DevTab.approve-error.test.ts:21 The rule is local, about one function's call shape, so a bounded window over the approve() body can decide it.
app/features/tools/devcases/DevTab.approve-error.test.ts:27 The failure message names the in-tree remedy as a literal, and the reader can act on it from the file they are editing.
